jobs.occupation: Data Architect - Global Data & Analytics Platform
jobs.description:
About the job
As a Data Architect, you will shape the future architecture of Alfa Laval's Global Data & Analytics Platform. You will work across business domains, source systems, data products and technical teams to create a connected, scalable and governed data landscape. Combining strategic architecture with hands-on data modelling, you will assess the current landscape, define the target architecture and help teams bridge the gap between the current and future states. 
 
Alfa Laval's global data landscape spans research and development, sales, service, operations, supply chain, finance, HR and sustainability, with data distributed across multiple source systems and structures. You will collaborate with business stakeholders, enterprise and solution architects, data product teams, developers and platform engineers to establish common standards, models and architectural principles. Your work will make enterprise data easier to find, understand, integrate and reuse, creating a scalable foundation for reporting, analytics, digital products and AI. 
 
Key responsibilities 
Define and drive a coherent data architecture for Alfa Laval's Global Data & Analytics Platform-creating one connected architectural direction across business domains, systems, products and value streams, including ERP, CRM and domain-specific solutions. 
Establish and promote common architectural principles, standards and guardrails for data modelling, governance, integration, interoperability, security, quality, scalability and reuse across the platform. 
Shape the target architecture and roadmap by assessing the current landscape, identifying gaps and dependencies, and defining practical steps towards a unified future state. 
Create and maintain consistent, reusable data models across business domains, supporting common definitions and enabling data to be used across multiple analytics and business use cases. 
Translate business requirements into enterprise-level data architecture, ensuring that data products and platform capabilities align with the overall architecture rather than creating isolated solutions. 
Work hands-on with architects, data engineers and developers to implement data models, integration patterns and shared platform capabilities. 
Partner with business and technical stakeholders to align priorities, explain architectural decisions, resolve trade-offs and build support across organizational boundaries. 
Collaborate with other architects and evaluate technologies to ensure the platform can support future analytics, AI and digital business needs. 

 
Who are you
You are a strategic and hands-on data architect who is comfortable working with ambiguity, navigating complex organizations and making decisions with incomplete information. You are pragmatic and structured, with a focus on implementable outcomes and long-term business value. Rather than creating isolated solutions, you are motivated by building reusable capabilities that can support the organization over time. You are curious and forward-looking, while remaining grounded in practical delivery. 
 
You build strong working relationships with business and technical stakeholders and are comfortable working with people at different levels and in different disciplines. You explain complex architectural topics clearly and practically, facilitate discussions, create alignment across organizational silos, and use communication and influencing skills to drive change. You are collaborative and approachable, while also being prepared to constructively challenge existing assumptions and approaches when this helps create better outcomes across a global, matrixed organization. 
 
What you know
To succeed in this role, you bring strong experience in data architecture and modelling, combined with the technical expertise needed to shape and implement scalable cloud-based data platforms. We believe you have: 
At least five years of experience in data architecture, enterprise data architecture, data platform architecture or a related senior data role. 
Proven experience designing and implementing modern cloud-based data and analytics architectures in enterprise environments, preferably using Microsoft Azure and Azure data services. 
Strong experience in conceptual, logical and physical data modelling, including translating business requirements into data architecture and implementable data models. 
Ability to balance platform standardization with domain autonomy, enabling reusable data products while supporting business-specific needs. 
Experience designing data integration, transformation and orchestration solutions, including enterprise integration patterns and cross-system data flows. 
Experience defining target architecture, architectural principles, standards and implementation roadmaps. 
Experience working with enterprise data platforms, data products, including data mesh or similar distributed data concepts. 
Hands-on experience with Databricks, Unity Catalog, SQL, Python/PySpark and Power BI, or similar tools. 
Experience with data governance, access models, data quality, metadata management and data security. 
Experience working across multiple business domains, products or value streams. 
Experience working with both technical delivery teams and senior business stakeholders. 
Fluent English, both written and spoken. 

 
It is considered an advantage if you have: 
Experience working across business domains such as ERP, CRM, supply chain, finance or manufacturing. 
Experience supporting analytics, machine learning or AI use cases. 
Experience with cloud-based data platforms, particularly Microsoft Azure. 
Experience in a large, global and matrixed organization.

Qualifications

jobs.occupation: Grants Officer for the Africa Region
jobs.description:
About the Tenure Facility
The Tenure Facility is the first and only international financial mechanism exclusively focused on securing land and forest rights for Indigenous Peoples and local communities worldwide. Recognizing and upholding these rights represents one of the most impactful opportunities for fostering sustainable rural development, achieving global climate goals, and mitigating local conflicts in a cost-effective manner.
Through grants and technical assistance, the Tenure Facility empowers Indigenous Peoples and local communities by strengthening their capacity to implement land and forest tenure reforms. Additionally, it supports governments in testing and scaling innovative approaches to land rights recognition, ensuring practical solutions to administrative and legal challenges.
Overview of the Position
The Grants Officer reports to the Chief Operating Officer and forms part of the Operations Team. The Grants Officer plays a key role in the implementation of the Tenure Facility’s grant-making and grant supervision processes. He or she will be responsible for administering the grant processes of the Tenure Facility’s projects and for ensuring that Tenure Facility staff members, consultants, and project partners operate within existing policies, guidelines, and procedures.
While the position falls under the Operations Team, given its strong programmatic focus, the Grants Officer is expected to work in close coordination with the Program Officers and the Finance Unit. The position may involve in-country visits to project partners.
Overarching Responsibilities
Contribute to establishing the Tenure Facility as a highly credible and respected foundation among international development institutions and donors.
Generate mutual trust and respect with Indigenous Peoples and local communities and their cultures, with full awareness of the intricacies of relationships among them and their allies and supporters.
Contribute to a collaborative and resilient internal working culture that supports sustained progress toward the Tenure Facility’s strategic goals and objectives.

Specific Responsibilities
The main responsibilities include:
Ensure that data related to grants and grantees in the Project Management System (Roots) is complete and meets Tenure Facility standards.
Work with Program Officers to provide prompt and sensitive responses to all unsolicited requests for funding and record related information.
Track the progress of project preparation, implementation, disbursement, reporting, and closure in Roots, and prepare related reports for management, donors, communications, and other stakeholders.
Coordinate the procurement of consultants and programme-related services, assist in preparing consultant contracts, ensure compliance with foundation regulations, and handle related queries, invoices, and payments.
Draft grant management documents, such as grant agreements, extensions, and amendments, for review by Program Officers and Financial Controllers, and manage related correspondence with grantees.
Review grant concept notes, proposals, risk registers, quality assurance reviews, and grant agreements to ensure they are complete and aligned with Tenure Facility policies.
Ensure the timely submission and approval of grantee reports by tracking and monitoring their status and sending reminders to grantees.
Shepherd grants and contracts through the review and approval process.
Assist with grant payment schedules, disbursements, and monitoring grant balances in coordination with Financial Controllers.
Assist with programme-related travel preparations and ensure reports are created and registered in TF systems.
Train new programme staff on grants and contracts processes and the use of the Project Management System (Roots).
Advise Tenure Facility staff members, consultants, and grantees on policies and procedures related to grant management.
Work to enhance and improve grants management processes and increase efficiency.
Undertake special projects as assigned.

Qualifications and Requirements
University degree (Bachelor’s degree or equivalent) in international development, law, business or public administration, social sciences, natural resource management, or a related field. A Master’s degree is an asset.
Minimum of 3 to 5 years of relevant professional experience in grants management, programme operations or administration, or project management, preferably with a foundation, international NGO, donor agency, or similar organisation.
Experience working with partners in Africa, and with Indigenous Peoples and local communities, is a strong asset.
Experience with grants management or similar information systems; familiarity with NGO Online (DigiPING) is an asset.
Fluency in English and French, both written and spoken, is required.
Fluency in Portuguese and/or Spanish would be considered an asset.
Willingness and ability to travel regularly, including to project sites and partner organisations in Africa, sometimes in remote locations.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and online collaboration tools.
Ability to work independently and as part of a multicultural, geographically distributed team, with cultural sensitivity and respect for Indigenous Peoples and local communities.

Terms of Employment
Permanent full-time position, starting 7 January 2027, with a six months' probationary period.
Location: Kungsholmen, Stockholm.
Collective agreement, pension and insurance: Almega Tjänstemannaavtalet.
Salary by agreement.

 
The Tenure Facility promotes a balanced, diverse workforce, a strength that helps us better understand and address our partners' needs, and we continually strive to improve our gender balance.

As the organization's foremost automation expert, you will provide technical direction, establish engineering standards, and guide key architectural decisions. A significant part of your role will be fostering technical excellence within the automation team through mentoring, coaching, and knowledge sharing. You will help build a strong automation capability that supports current product development and future innovation. While your primary focus will be automation and control systems, you will work closely with colleagues in software development, electronics, product management, and other engineering teams to ensure successful integration and alignment across solutions. This is a technical leadership role without formal personnel responsibility based on-site in Helsingborg.
Profile and experience
To be successful in this role you need
At least 8 years of experience in industrial automation, control systems, or Operational Technology, with several years in a senior technical role.
Deep expertise in industrial automation and control systems, including automation architecture, PLC-based control systems, industrial communication, HMI solutions, functional safety, and the development of robust, scalable automation platforms.
Being comfortable making architectural decisions and balancing immediate product needs with long-term technical strategy.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills in both Swedish and English
Swedish citizenship. The position is security-classified and requires security vetting, including a background check.

Experience leading technical initiatives, influencing engineering direction and working with stakeholders and requirements is highly valued. Experience with Schneider EAE or IEC 61499 is an advantage but not required.
We are looking for someone passionate about automation and engineering excellence. You are curious, pragmatic, and energized by solving challenging technical problems while continuously improving products and ways of working. With a deep technical knowledge and strong collaboration skills, you bring structure, credibility, and a long-term perspective while remaining hands-on when needed. With a natural ability to lead through expertise and influence you truly enjoy developing people, sharing knowledge, and creating an environment where engineers can grow and perform at their best.
Apply today In this recruitment process Nederman collaborates with Mpya Sci & Tech. For questions about the position, you are welcome to contact Recruitment Consultant Christian Billberg on 0731-489 875. We review applications on a rolling basis so do not hesitate to apply via www.mpyascitech.com as soon as possible, as the position may be filled before the final application date.

jobs.occupation: 5G RAN System Engineer / Baseband System Developer
jobs.description:

We believe in transparency, trust and giving people the freedom and responsibility to grow. Our consultants should feel that they are part of something, have a real influence and are rewarded for the value they create.
At TECHLA, technology matters – but people matter even more. We believe the best results come from skilled people who take ownership, work closely together and genuinely care about what they deliver.
We are big enough to deliver, but small enough to care.

Design and specification of algorithms within RAN/Baseband

We believe you have
Experience from 5G RAN, Baseband or similar telecom systems
 Good understanding of 3GPP-based communication systems, such as 3G, 4G/LTE and 5G NR
 Experience from the lower layers of the protocol stack, such as L1/L2, PHY or MAC
 Knowledge within communication theory, signal processing or radio algorithms
 Experience from system work, algorithm design, technical analysis or performance optimization
 The ability to understand complex technical problems and drive them forward
 Good English skills, both spoken and written

It is meritorious if you have
Previous experience from Ericsson, Combitech or another RAN/Baseband-related environment

Company description:
At Epiroc, innovation is at the core of everything we do. Our vision is clear: we aim to accelerate the transformation of mining towards a greener and more sustainable industry. In this role, you’ll get the opportunity to work with state-of-the-art mobile machines, electric drivetrains, and control systems that are moving towards higher degrees of automation and sophistication.

Join our team 
Our aspiration is to produce the world’s greenest machines using the world’s greenest materials. We are leading the charge towards a more sustainable future through battery-electric, zero-emission mining equipment. Are you ready to be part of this journey? Join our fantastic team of engineers and play a pivotal role in advancing mining technology while pushing boundaries on performance, reliability, and efficiency.

Your mission as a system engineer is to develop and adapt our machine systems in terms of hardware, system architecture, and functionality to fulfill requirements regarding e.g., performance, availability, and safety. You also have a solid understanding of software, including control systems and system architectures, as well as CAN communication protocols (J1939, CAN Open). Knowledge of software development and electrical systems, and experience with CAD, simulation, and other software tools are considered a plus.

Life at Epiroc 
By joining our team, you can expect an atmosphere of creativity, innovation, and workplace diversity. You will be a part of a group of skilled and helpful colleagues who live by our core values: Collaboration, Commitment, and Innovation. We work in a global environment with 120 different nationalities! 
In addition to the fact that we have a culture that is characterized by development combined with having a good balance between work and leisure, there are some things that makes us a little extra proud to work at Epiroc:   
Global career opportunities, Epiroc University, for your own competence development, Community involvement, benefits package, which amongst other things include flexible working hours and bonus. 
Life at Epiroc can include the possibility for a hybrid workplace. It is a way of working that offers flexibility to partly work from home, based on your role, responsibilities, and individual conditions.  
Location and travel 
This position is located in Örebro, Sweden.

Solid foundational understanding of control engineering, mechatronic systems, or thermodynamic processes.

Quintus Technologies specializes in the design, manufacturing, installation and support of high-pressure systems for sheet metal forming, advanced materials densification for high-quality industrial components as well as high pressure processing for food and beverage to deactivate the bacteria.

Are you highly motivated and young specialist in reconstructive plastic surgery eager to join our dedicated team of surgeons? Take the opportunity to become a microsurgery fellow at Karolinska University Hospital, Sweden! As part of our team, you will engage in all aspects of clinical work, research, and education alongside our staff surgeons and residents.
What we offer
Access to state-of-the-art surgical facilities and technologies
Mentorship and guidance from internationally recognized experts in microsurgery.
Opportunities to contribute to high-impact research.
Exposure to a wide range of complex cases at a world-class teaching hospital
A collaborative and innovative learning environment
Competitive salary – approx. €4500/month plus compensation for late surgeries

About the Fellowship
Karolinska University Hospital, one of the world’s leading medical centers, ranked 4th best hospital globally and 13th in terms of innovation, is offering an exciting Microsurgery Fellowship. Our department is renowned for cutting-edge work and innovation in reconstructive microsurgery, with a strong commitment to excellence in patient care, research, and education.
Our department performs microsurgical reconstructions for a broad spectrum of patients, including those with cancer, trauma, and transgender individuals. We perform 120–150 free tissue transfers annually and a large number of pedicled flaps every week. Our work is carried out in close collaboration with several medical disciplines at both a Level 1 trauma center and a comprehensive cancer center, with regular multidisciplinary conferences
This fellowship provides advanced training in a wide range of reconstructive microsurgical procedures, including but not limited to:
Free flap reconstruction for head and neck reconstruction
Breast reconstruction
Trauma-related reconstructive surgery
Sarcoma reconstruction
Advanced burn reconstruction
Gender-affirming surgery – phalloplasty
Lymphatic microsurgery

As a fellow, you will work closely with our expert surgeons, gaining hands-on experience in both elective and emergency microsurgical procedures. You will be involved in all aspects of patient care, from preoperative planning to postoperative management. The fellowship also includes opportunities for clinical research.
Number of fellowships offered: 2 with separate starting dates
Planned start of fellowship: Mid-August/early September 2027, or March 2028
Duration: 6 months
Key Responsibilities
Assist and actively participate in advanced microsurgical procedures under supervision
Participate in preoperative and postoperative patient care
Collaborate with a multidisciplinary team, including surgeons, oncologists, and radiologists
Conduct research and contribute to ongoing clinical studies in microsurgery
Present cases and participate in weekly departmental meetings and seminars
Contribute to the training of plastic surgery residents and those rotating from other fields.

Requirements
Board certification or eligibility in Plastic Surgery (or equivalent)
Experience in microsurgery is preferred; however, training will be provided. Please include a description of your microsurgical experience
Documented interest in education, such as mentoring younger colleagues or medical students
Strong interest in both academic and clinical work
Fluency in English (Swedish is an advantage but not required)

Interested candidates should submit the following:
A detailed CV
A personal statement outlining your interest in microsurgery and career goals
Two letters of recommendation from academic or clinical mentors

Do you enjoy solving complex engineering challenges and using simulations to influence product development before physical testing begins?
At Thule, we develop products that inspire an active life. In this role, you will use advanced structural simulations to help shape product design, improve performance, and ensure our products meet high standards of safety, quality, and durability.

What you bring

You have a solid understanding of engineering principles, simulation methodologies, and product development processes. Experience with verification and validation activities, including the relationship between virtual and physical testing, is also an advantage.
As a person, you are self-driven, proactive, and collaborative, with a strong ability to take initiative and move work forward. You communicate technical insights effectively, enjoy working across functions, and are motivated by solving complex challenges, continuous improvement, and knowledge sharing. To succeed in this role, you are fluent in English, both written and spoken.

What we do
We are passionate believers in the power of education to transform people’s lives. We help students finding, applying to and enrolling in the right study program. Our multi-sided platforms help over 100 million prospective students every year find their ideal match among thousands of partner institutions, across a global network of hundreds of student websites.
It is a complicated and diverse problem space. We work hard to understand the needs of each student and each institution, and use technology and data to recommend the best matches for both.

About the role
Our Data & Insights squad builds the data products that Keystone runs on. These include analytics and reporting tools that help education providers measure and improve their recruitment performance, a shared data platform and business KPIs for leadership, and AI-supported tools for creating and publishing program and institution content.
You will decide what that engineering team builds and in which order. You will turn the strategic direction set by management into a roadmap the squad can deliver.
The role starts as Product Owner and is designed to grow. The aim is for you to become a full Product Manager from around month 9, owning a product area outright.
What you will do
Own one prioritised backlog across all Data & Insights products, refined weekly with the Engineering Manager and readable by anyone.
Take each product owner’s outcomes into quarterly planning and leave with a plan the engineering team has sized and agreed.
Decide on priority conflicts between stakeholders during the quarter and keep a decision log with the reason and owner for every pause, trade-off and change.
Write clear acceptance criteria for every epic and decide whether delivered work meets them. Communicate releases to stakeholders.
Manage product risks, such as scope, priority and dependencies on other business areas, and make priority decisions on blockers quickly.
Run a regular sync with the product owners that ends with the order of work written down.
Keep the squad’s roadmap and OKRs up to date and visible to leadership.
Track adoption, usage and performance of the data products, and iterate based on what you learn.
Gather feedback from customers and internal users to shape what comes next.

What success looks like
First 30 days
The backlog is in one place and ordered, and you take part in the squad ceremonies to keep work moving forward.

By month 6
The squad hits its delivery targets, with most work delivered on time against the quarterly plan and little scope change after it is locked.
You write the squad’s quarterly objectives rather than collecting them.

From month 9
You own adoption and outcome metrics for at least one product, likely the shared data platform.
You step into the Product Manager role for that area.

2+ years as a Product Owner, Product Manager or similar, working daily with engineers on a shared backlog.

Experience serving several stakeholders who each believe they come first and saying no to some of them in a way they accept.
A structured, precise way of writing requirements and prioritising.

Clear written and spoken English. Most decisions here travel by Jira, Confluence and email.

Where you will work
This is a hybrid role in Stockholm or Sheffield. Hybrid means you work from home and from the office every week, and we expect you to be in the office at least two days per week.
Why join us?
Take ownership of data products that directly impact customers and internal teams.
A clear path from Product Owner to Product Manager.
Work in a small, focused team with high visibility and responsibility.
Join a mission-driven, international company with hybrid working.

What is the team like?
You will be part of the Product team, working day to day with our in-house engineering team, within a larger product and tech team of 20+ engineers, product managers and designers from diverse backgrounds and experiences.
Collaborative, ambitious and driven best describes us. You will join a strong team with great chemistry, who are passionate about what they do and always go the extra mile. Read more about us at https://www.keg.com/

Company description: Your future team 
Software & Simulation Factory (SSF) is a centralized organization within Volvo Group, responsible for embedded software across multiple business areas, including trucks, buses, marine, and construction equipment. We support the full software lifecycle for both real-time and service-oriented domains, from hosting, infrastructure, and developer experience to continuous integration, testing, automation, and continuous delivery and deployment
 Job description:    
 How you’ll contribute 
As a Software Delivery & Integration Engineer you will establish a common global way of working with continuous delivery and deployment of embedded software and calibration artifacts, while developing in-house solutions for software calibrations.  You will work with passionate and experienced colleagues providing SW integration and delivery capabilities to better serve Volvo Group's customers. This role gives you the opportunity to work hands-on with the development of our SW calibration and integration systems and solutions, while collaborating with stakeholders across the global Volvo Group network. 
 We are in a digital transformation phase, and the shift towards software-defined vehicles puts new requirements on our SW integration, delivery flows, and systems. We need to build back-end architecture that meets Volvo Group's customer needs, with one common denominator: doing as much as possible as early as possible in the flow. In this role, you will be instrumental in understanding and interpreting stakeholder and customer needs, and in proactively suggesting and introducing changes based on that understanding.
 Key responsibilities: 
  Lead software delivery and deployment infrastructure, ensuring reliable and efficient integration processes and strategies. 
 Develop in-house calibration application and drive AI integration across software and calibration processes. 
 Build and share domain knowledge in software and calibration tools and processes, both locally and across the global organization.
  Who are you? 
We are looking for someone with a strong transformation and collaborative mindset who is eager to learn, explore, and understand the business. You thrive in dynamic environments, embrace new challenges and ambiguity, and take ownership of your own development and growth. With strong analytical skills, you take initiatives and drive tasks forward with determination while bringing fresh perspectives and innovative ideas to the team.You enjoy building relationships and leveraging a global network to create impact while working collaboratively across teams and functions. In addition, you contribute to a culture of continuous learning by actively sharing knowledge, exchanging insights, and supporting the development of others. 
 You have a passion for programming, software, and AI, who brings strong social skills, equally comfortable writing code, and seeing the bigger system context. You enjoy being the connector who spots patterns and ties people and ideas together. The role offers the opportunity to travel to different sites around the world, building contacts you can draw on to help lead technology development at home, working with stakeholders abroad. You're comfortable translating customer needs into code, asking what a requirement actually means in practice.  
 Requirements: 
  Bachelor or Master of Science in Software Engineering, Information Technology, Computer Science, Physics, Artificial Intelligence, Automotive engineering or a related field.  
 Hands-on experience in Python  
   
To qualify for the Graduate program, you: 
  Have completed a Bachelors/master’s degree prior to the start of the program but not more than 3 years ago.
 Should not have more than three years' full-time relevant working experience in the field prior to starting, excluding part-time work during studies.  
 Are fluent in English, both written and verbal.   
 Are willing to travel and participate in international short-term assignments

  An opportunity to work with the latest technology.
 An exciting and global working environment with experienced colleagues.
 Possibility to gain international experience through a short-term assignment abroad.
 A competitive salary and permanent position from day one.
 Various workshops and seminars designed to help you grow into your future career at Volvo Group.
 The possibility to shape your own career with endless career opportunities.
